name: Exercise 2.3: Learn How RACI Connects People and Process

content.text: Now that we understand the full architecture of business processes, we need a practical way to manage who does what within each process. That's where RACI comes in.
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Now that we understand the full architecture of business processes, we need a practical way to manage who does what within each process. That's where RACI comes in.

content.text: What is RACI?
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: What is RACI?

content.text: RACI is a responsibility assignment framework that brings clarity to process roles. The acronym stands for:
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: RACI is a responsibility assignment framework that brings clarity to process roles. The acronym stands for:

content.text: R – Responsible
: The person who actually does the work to achieve the task
A – Accountable
: The person who is ultimately answerable for the completion and quality of the deliverable (there should be only ONE accountable person for each task)
C – Consulted
: People whose opinions are sought during the process (two-way communication)
I – Informed
: People who are kept up-to-date on progress (one-way communication)

content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Here’s what a RACI chart (or matrix) looks like:

content.text: Why RACI Matters
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Why RACI Matters

content.text: Without clear responsibility assignment:
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Without clear responsibility assignment:

content.text: Tasks fall through the cracks ("I thought someone else was handling that")
Multiple people duplicate efforts on the same task
Decision-making becomes slow or stalled
Accountability becomes impossible to enforce
RACI provides a simple but powerful framework to eliminate these issues. It also gives us a great framework to work with when we look at how AI can take over certain elements of process.
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: RACI provides a simple but powerful framework to eliminate these issues. It also gives us a great framework to work with when we look at how AI can take over certain elements of process.

content.text: Implementing RACI in Your Business
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Implementing RACI in Your Business

content.text: For each process in your business, you'll (eventually) need to identify:
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: For each process in your business, you'll (eventually) need to identify:

content.text: The key activities or tasks within that process
The roles involved in that process
Who is R, A, C, and I for each task
Don’t worry, this is a long-term goal!
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Don’t worry, this is a long-term goal!

content.text: However, for now, we do want to identify who is currently
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: However, for now, we do want to identify who is currently

content.text: accountable
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: accountable

content.text: for each process, and if the process currently doesn't exist in your business. This itself is valuable information—it highlights potential gaps in your business process architecture.
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: for each process, and if the process currently doesn't exist in your business. This itself is valuable information—it highlights potential gaps in your business process architecture.

content.text: If a process does not currently exist in your organization, you can mark it as “Accountable: N/A” if it legitimately isn't needed in your business model at this stage.  If it doesn’t exist, but it represents a gap that needs to be filled in the near-term, you can mark it as “Accountable: Future.”
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: If a process does not currently exist in your organization, you can mark it as “Accountable: N/A” if it legitimately isn't needed in your business model at this stage.  If it doesn’t exist, but it represents a gap that needs to be filled in the near-term, you can mark it as “Accountable: Future.”

content.text: Remember: The goal isn't to implement every possible process immediately, but to understand your current state and prioritize improvements that will deliver the most value.
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Remember: The goal isn't to implement every possible process immediately, but to understand your current state and prioritize improvements that will deliver the most value.

content.text: Instructor note
content.circle_ios_fallback_text: Instructor note

content.text: : We’ll be adopting RACI as an accountability framework, but will focus on the Responsible, Accountable, and Consulted roles, ignoring the Informed category since any number of people can be informed about a process without it impacting how that process functions.
